content.content:
# Running tests

**track**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testFast`.

**shard**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testSystem`. Shard i of n takes every n-th file of the sorted list, from index i.

**code state**
: Code of a tree as one edit leaves it. Only an edit of code makes a new code state; a commit does not.

## The two suites

`ant testFast` runs about 1,800 tests in four tracks at once, in about 9 to 11 minutes:

- compiler: `CompilerJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/` and `parser_tests/`. It is the longest track, so it sets the total time.
- library: `LibraryJUTest` over `library_tests/`.
- othercompiler: `OtherCompilerJUTest` over `other_compiler_tests/`.
- misc: the unit `*JUTest` classes.

`ant testSystem` runs `SystemJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, the interpreter's test folder. It runs about 500 tests in four shards, in about 2 to 4 minutes.

`ant testSpecData` runs the specification's 130 extracted examples (`SpecData/examples/basic`, `preliminaries`, `advanced`) under walk, in under a minute. The gate runs it after the two suites.

The newest gate summary has the exact counts and times of the last landed run:

    git log -1 --name-only --format= -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt'

The two suites work in the same way:

- Each suite runs `ant compileAll` first, as every `ant` test target does, so it never tests stale classes. After an edit of Java or Scala, that build empties `default_repository/caches` (`build-and-caches.md`, "Building"). Each analyses or compiles the Fortress code that it tests, in private caches.
- Each JVM gets 768 MB, a 32 MB stack and `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, whatever the shell exports. The run steps of the compiled tests get `JAVA_FLAGS=-Xmx4g -Xss64m`, also whatever the shell exports.
- Each suite deletes `ProjectFortress/test-caches` when it starts. Each JVM keeps its caches in a folder of its own under it, so that the JVMs do not overwrite each other's entries. Temporary files go to `ProjectFortress/test-tmp/`.
- The results are in `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-<track>/` and `system-<i>/`, as `TEST-<class>.txt`.

To run a suite:

- Run one suite at a time in a tree, because each suite deletes the `test-caches` that the other uses.
- Read the verdict in the line before `Total time:`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` means zero failures, and `BUILD FAILED` means at least one. Every `ant` test target ends with these lines, and exits non-zero when it failed.
- To compare test counts, compare the sum of the four shards. A file added to `tests/` moves every later file to another shard.
- If a suite's count fell, a `.test` file or a `tests=` line almost always went missing.

## The switches that the harness reads

Put a `-D` switch on the `java` line of a run by hand; the `java` line in `harness-one.sh` is a model. On the `ant` line, it does not reach the suites' JVMs.

- `-Dtests=<dir>`: the folder that `SystemJUTest` runs, in place of `tests/`.
- `-Dfortress.suite.shard=i/n`: run shard i of n only.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.count=N`: run N files at most.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.seed=<value>`: the order of the files. Each run prints its seed as `FORTRESS_UNITTESTS_SEED=...`.
- `FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1` for `SystemJUTest`, `-Dfortress.junit.verbose=true` for the compiled tests' classes: show the output of passing tests too.
- `-Dfortress.junit.reset=false`: `CompilerJUTest` and `LibraryJUTest` keep their caches folder. Without it, they empty it when they start.

## Outside the gate

- `ant testNotPassing` runs the interpreter programs of `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet/`, which are expected to fail. It fails if one of them passes.
- Nothing runs these folders: `not_working_compiler_tests/`, `not_working_library_tests/`, `not_working_static_tests/`, `obsolete_interpreter_tests/`, `long_term_not_working/`, `linker_tests/`, `compiler_regressions/`. Put every new test in a gated test folder. A test of a defect that fails today is an `XXX` test there (`tests-writing.md`).

## When to run a whole suite

- The gate runs every suite once, on the tree that lands (`gate.md`). Your brief says whether you run the gate.
- If your edit changes the Java or Scala of the checker, of walk or of a phase that both paths share, run all the tests that it reaches. Run them once, after your last edit of code. The run needs no commit.
  - For the checker, run `ant testQuick`: the compiler, othercompiler and library tracks at once (below).
  - For walk, run `ant testSystem`. It is the same as its four shards run by hand.
  - For a shared phase (under `compiler/`: name binding, DSL grammars, desugaring, the marking of overloaded calls in `OverloadRewriter`) or the parser, run both.
- Quote the verdict lines and the command in your report, with the commit if your code is committed.
- If the gate later runs on a tree that holds other changes too, that tree is another code state. Your run and the gate's run do not repeat each other.
- After an edit of the code generator (`codegen/`, `OverloadSet`) or the run time (`runtimeSystem/`), run your own tests, and the four-thread atomic runs (`gate.md`) if `compiler.md` asks for them. Leave the whole tracks to the gate.
- After every other change, run only your own tests, through the scripts below. Leave the rest to the gate. This includes an edit of either library, though it reaches many tests.

The suites do not check these:

- the bytecode optimizer, which nothing in the compiler calls;
- DSL grammars, except one program whose phases the misc track runs: `syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss`;
- the linker's aliasing of apis;
- `fortress unparse`;
- the round trip of the `.tfi` and `.tfs` caches;
- a behaviour above one thread that one run of each suite at four threads does not hit.

If your edit is in one of these, your own tests are its only check. Say so in your report.

## One test, or a few

Each script and `fortress junit` below ends with the verdict of JUnit's text runner: `OK (n tests)`, or `FAILURES!!!` with the counts. Read the verdict there: the exit code is 0 whatever the verdict.

### Interpreter tests

Run interpreter tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/`) from the tree's root, after you set up the call:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh <tree>/tmp/h1 \
        ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss [ProjectFortress/tests/X.test] [more files ...]

- It runs `SystemJUTest` with testSystem's JVM settings, at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, on a folder that holds only the files that you name.
- It keeps its cache in the folder `<scratch-dir>.cache`. It starts from that cache while the build and the library sources are those that filled it. Otherwise, or with `COLD_CACHE=1`, it starts empty. Its first line says `cache filled` or `cache empty`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing. After you edit Java, Scala or a parser grammar, run `ant compileAll` first. If your tree has no build, seed it or build it as `worktrees.md` says.
- Give it a scratch directory that holds nothing else. The script deletes the directory when it starts and when it ends.
- If a test has an `X.test` file (its keys for a refusal at load), name it beside its `X.fss`.
- It takes 15 to 25 s with an empty cache, mostly to analyse the library, and about 4 s with a filled one. Name several files in one call to run them in one JVM.
- It shows the output of passing tests too, and removes the Java stack frames.

To see the whole diagnostic, with its Java stack, run the program directly, from `ProjectFortress/` as the harness does, because an import is looked up in the current directory first:

    cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress -debug stacktrace tests/X.fss

The direct run and the harness use different heaps (`interpreter.md`, "Running a program").

### Compiled tests

Compiled tests are the `.test` files in `compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` and `other_compiler_tests/`. They link with the library's jars in the tree's `default_repository/caches`. If a build started the caches again, or the tree's caches are empty, run the library order first (`build-and-caches.md`).

The script is `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`. `climb-batch-N` is the folder's real name, not a placeholder. Run your own tree's copy: it runs the tree that it is in.

    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh <label> \
        ProjectFortress/compiler_tests X.test Y.test > <tree>/tmp/junit-<label>.txt 2>&1

- `<label>` is any word. It marks the run's lines in the output. The script writes to standard output only, so redirect it to your `tmp/`.
- With `ONE_JVM=1`, the whole list runs in one `fortress junit` run, in one JVM. The compile and link tests run before the run tests, as in the suite. Without `ONE_JVM=1`, each file gets its own JVM.
- It removes the named components' entries from the tree's `default_repository/caches` before the whole list and after it, not between files. So a link test and the run test that uses its jar pass in one call, with or without `ONE_JVM=1`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing, as `harness-one.sh` does.
- It removes the Java stack frames, and cuts each line at 240 characters.
- Its JVMs keep their temporary files in the tree's `tmp/`, and run at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`.

To run the same list in one JVM without the script, and without its removal of cache entries:

    cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress junit compiler_tests/X.test compiler_tests/Y.test

Run all the new files of one test folder together, in one JVM, as the suite does. A test that passes alone can fail beside others.

## One unit-test class, or one track

To run one unit-test class: `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=BitsJUTest`. It uses the tree's own caches and the shell's `FORTRESS_THREADS`.

To run tracks of testFast whole, run their target. Each target runs its tracks as testFast does, with the same JVMs and private caches:

- `ant testCompiler`: the compiler and othercompiler tracks.
- `ant testOtherCompiler`: the othercompiler track.
- `ant testLibrary`: the library track.
- `ant testQuick`: the three tracks.
# The gate

The gate runs the seven steps below on one tree, in about 25 minutes. It is green if every step passes, and red if one fails. If a step fails, run the rest, so that the summary holds every step's result.

## What it writes

The summary, `summary.txt`, has one tab-separated row for each suite: `track/suite`, tests, failures, errors, skipped. Below the rows, lines that start with `#` give each log's `BUILD` and `Total time:` lines, the machine that ran the gate (`# machine`), the atomic runs and the ladder's comparison. A landed summary can also end with `# microgpt-walk` lines: the `VERDICT:` and `rc=` lines of the microGPT walk check (`interpreter.md`, "The model program"), run on the landed tree. Add them only if your brief asks for the microGPT walk check on the landed tree.

If your brief asks you to land a gate's results, put them in a new `gate/` folder in `explorations/compile-ladder/`, under the `climb-batch-` name that your brief gives, in the form of the newest one: `summary.txt`, and in `ladder/` the files `ladder.tsv`, `microgpt-phase.md`, `comparison.txt` and `microgpt-comparison.txt`. The next gate compares with the newest summary there or in `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/`, and finds no other. Land them in a commit that changes nothing else that the gate reads.

Steps 5 and 7 use shell functions that `explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh` defines. The file runs nothing. In each Bash call of steps 5 and 7, set up the call as `build-and-caches.md` says, which sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the tree's root. Then source the file, from the root:

    source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh

## When to run it

Your brief says whether you run the gate. If it does not ask, run only your own tests (`tests-running.md`).

If it asks, first check whether the newest gate still holds for your tree. A gate's tables stay valid until the tree changes under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or in `build.xml`, outside the test files. A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` file directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory. The commit that landed the newest summary changed nothing that the gate reads. Commit your tree, then run this command. It prints each path, test files excepted, changed since that commit:

    G=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt')
    git diff --name-only $G HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml \
        | grep -v -E '^ProjectFortress/([^/]*_)?tests/[^/]*\.(fss|fsi|test)$'

- If it prints a path, run the gate.
- If not, the newest gate holds. Run only the changed test files, through `harness-one.sh` and `junit.sh` (`tests-running.md`).

## The steps

Run these steps from the tree's root. Keep the logs of steps 2 and 4 in `tmp/gate/`, as `compileAll.txt`, `testFast.txt`, `testSystem.txt` and `testSpecData.txt`.

1. Read the Avail column of `df -h /`. Warning: deleting `/tmp/fortress*rats` can break other live runs. If the column shows less than 1 GB, delete `/tmp/fortress*rats`, `ProjectFortress/test-tmp` and `ProjectFortress/test-caches`, and read it again. If it still shows less than 500 MB, stop and report.
2. Run `rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS tmp/gate && mkdir -p tmp/gate`, then `ant compileAll`.
3. If the build printed `Caches <tree>/default_repository/caches started again, empty`, run the library order (`build-and-caches.md`). If not, and a source of the compiler's library changed since the caches were filled, take its step in `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library". Then copy the caches twice for the ladder regression, before anything else compiles into them:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

4. Run `ant testFast`, then `ant testSystem`, then `ant testSpecData`. All three must have zero failures.
5. Write the summary: `gate_summary tmp/gate tmp/gate/summary.txt`. Compare it: `gate_compare "$(last_landed_summary)" tmp/gate/summary.txt`. It prints a line for a suite with failures or errors, a suite with no tests, a suite whose count of tests fell, and a suite that is gone. Each such line makes the gate red. A count that rose prints nothing.
6. Do the atomic runs, and append their lines to the summary.
7. Do the ladder regression.

## The atomic runs

The atomic runs compile fourteen programs, and run each one three times at four threads, in about a minute. They need the library's jars in the tree's caches (`build-and-caches.md`). Run them from `ProjectFortress/`:

    for p in AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG \
             atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 \
             nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2 ; do
      d=other_compiler_tests ; [ -f compiler_tests/$p.fss ] && d=compiler_tests
      timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile $d/$p.fss >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" ; continue ; }
      for i in 1 2 3 ; do
        out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$?
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && { out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$? ; }
        case "$out" in *FAIL*) r=FAIL ;; *PASS*) r=PASS ;; *) r="NO-PASS rc=$rc" ;; esac
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && r=TIMEOUT-TWICE
        echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 $r"
      done
    done

The gate is red on any FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE.

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

## Comparing with an earlier run

- `ant testSystem` runs in four shards, the summary's rows `system-0` to `system-3`. A shard takes the files by their place in a sorted list, so an added file moves every later file to another shard. When you compare by hand, compare only the sum of the four. `gate_compare` sums them.
- In printed output, mask only these differences: the `Operation took <n>ms` line, a Java line number in a stack frame, an object's identity hash (`@` and hex digits), and a position in a library file that your change moved. In your report, list each test with a masked difference, and the kinds masked in it.
- If your brief asks you to compare the interpreter tests with a base run, use the two scripts in `explorations/coordinator/tools/count-run/`. `count-run.sh` runs every `ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss` under walk, one JVM per test: run it once on the base commit and once after your edit. `compare-normalised.py` compares the two runs, with the last three masks above. Each script's header gives its usage.
# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push three times, in this order:

         git push origin main
         git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8
         git push origin main:blinded-fable

     The third push keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and say so in your report.

content.content:
# The report and the record

## What every report holds

Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.

A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.

A fact is a finding that is an established property of the tree, the language, the library or their tools, and that later work builds on. A defect also gets its ledger row, and a fact about it may cite the row.

A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.

Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:

- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
- **For FACTS.** Each fact that your work established, in the hand-over form of "Writing to the record". If your brief let you write FACTS, give instead the number of each entry that you added or rewrote. If your work established no fact, write "none".
- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.

## At a point to report

- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
- Then finish the work.
- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.

## Timings and citations

- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.

## POSITIONS and FACTS

POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.

Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".

## The gap ledger

The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).

A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.

- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.

Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.

Three limits of `ledger.py` (below):

- A row at its 1,200-character limit takes no further note.
- No command edits a row's claim. `close --claim` takes a corrected one.
- Its heading reader does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.

## Reading the record

Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:

    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh

- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.

A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.

Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:

    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE

## Writing to the record

- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`, never by hand. `add` gives a new entry its number, and `set` rewrites an entry. The tool writes the entry to `FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md`, and its earlier text to the history file beside it. It commits nothing: commit both files in one commit. Its header gives its usage.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, add each fact as a new entry in the section of its topic, in the commit that establishes it. Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers. Point the entry to that section, by your report's file and the section's heading. If your report is only your final message, hand the fact over instead. Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work.
- If your brief does not let you write FACTS, hand each fact over in the "For FACTS" item of your report, with:
  - the fact as it stands now, in one sentence;
  - what it means for the work;
  - the number that a decision rests on, if any, with what it counts; if its parts belong to different ledger rows, the part of each row;
  - the test that fails if the fact stops holding, or the command and the output that show it;
  - the section of your report that holds the detail.
- If your brief lets you write FACTS, rewrite a wrong entry in place. Otherwise say in your hand-over that the entry is wrong, with the evidence.
- POSITIONS holds each of the curator's decisions, in one place. Everything else points there. Write a decision there only if your brief gives it to you to record. If you have evidence against one, do as `exploring.md` says.
- Put new files of the work under `explorations/`. If you add a note directly in `explorations/` or `explorations/reviews/`, add its line to INDEX: ``- `PATH`: `` and the first sentence of the note's header comment.

Write the gap ledger only with `ledger.py`, which checks each line that it writes against the row template.

    L="python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py"

To add a row:

1. Print the row template, about 3 KB: `$T 'doc:explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md#The row template'`.
2. Write the row as one line in a file under your tree's `tmp/`, with `?` in its number cell.
3. Run `$L add FILE --section TITLE`. It numbers the row and puts it in that section. If the row breaks the template, it adds nothing and prints each rule broken. `$L sections` lists the titles.

To change a row:

- `$L note N TEXT` adds TEXT to the notes of row N.
- `$L duplicate N --of M` makes row N a pointer to row M.
- `$L close N --commit HASH --test NAME` marks row N `FIXED`, by the commit HASH and its test NAME. Run it once that commit is in `HEAD`, and commit the close after it.

## The repository's history

- The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository. Its trunk runs from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 and ends at `a874948ac`, the team's last commit.
- The commits after `a874948ac` are the revival's. After the tag `sealed-tree`, commit `75cca6683`, the revival began to fix the team's code, test first. Before it, the revival changed mainly the build and the toolchain.
- `git diff a874948ac -- FILE` shows what the revival changed in a file, and `git diff 75cca6683 -- FILE` what it changed after the tag.
- The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a `git log` of a directory stops at a cut and misses the team's earlier commits. Use `git log --follow` on a file, or compare contents.
- To find who wrote something, or where the repository's history after 2012 comes from, read `research/authorship.md` and `explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`.
- Commit `8fe1daa8f` copied a third-party port of the tree to Java 9 onto the team's last commit, `a874948ac`. Give its lines no credit, and name no author of it in any text that you commit. In a reconstruction of authorship, attribute nothing of it to anyone.
# The base build, seeded worktrees and the old code

**seeding**
: Making a worktree with a copy of the build and caches of a built, clean worktree. `seed-worktree.sh` makes the copy and rewrites the paths in it (`SKILL.md`, "The caches").

**base build**
: Clean worktree at the base, built in place by ant, or seeded. Every other worktree is seeded from it.

**old code**
: Base's code, run from the base build with a private caches folder.

Once the base build is built, run its code only as "Running the old code" says, with a private caches folder outside it. Any other run writes into the caches that every worktree is seeded from.

## Finding or building a base build

- If your brief names a base build, use it.
- If not, look in `git worktree list`. Earlier base builds are at paths such as `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`. A worktree can be your base build if it passes three checks:
  - `git -C <it> rev-parse HEAD` prints your base;
  - `git -C <it> status --porcelain` prints nothing;
  - it holds `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`.
- If no worktree passes them, build one at a path of your own, outside the main tree. It takes about 200 s: start the build and the library order detached, with the `nohup` line of `session.md`, "Long commands". `<base-commit>` is your base: the commit that your brief names, else your tree's `HEAD` when you start. Say so in your report.

      git worktree add --detach <base-build> <base-commit>
      cd <base-build>          # then set up the call as build-and-caches.md says
      ant compileAll
      # then the library order (build-and-caches.md), then this walk run, which warms walk's caches:
      bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
      git status --porcelain   # must print nothing: the seeding script refuses a base build that is not clean

If you check a fix against its old code, use a base build at the commit that the fix starts from. If a brief names the fix's base, the fix starts there. If not, the fix starts from `git merge-base <its branch> main`, or from the parent of its first commit on `main`.

## Seeding a worktree

A build, and a run of `bin/fortress` without a private caches folder, walk's too, write into the caches of the tree that they run in. So build and run only in a tree whose caches no other agent uses. Your brief says where you work. If your work builds or runs code and your brief gives you no tree of your own, seed a worktree of your own instead of building one. Then work only there.

Seeding takes about 3 s and 206 MB of disk. The new worktree runs walk and the compiled path right away, with the library already compiled.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh <base-build> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]

- The script checks out `<branch>`: a local branch, else origin's, else a new branch cut from `<start-point>`, by default the base build's commit. With `-`, it makes a detached worktree at `<start-point>`.
- If the script exits 2, the base build is not built or not clean, and the script made nothing. Then make the worktree with `git worktree add`, build it yourself, and say so in your report.
- If the worktree already exists, the script keeps its branch. If it already has a build, the script keeps that too. `SEED_FORCE=1` replaces it.
- If you start in a worktree that has no build, seed it in place: name it as `<new-worktree>`, and its branch as `<branch>`.
- The script lists the library sources that differ from the base build's commit. Before a compiled run, take for each the step that `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library", gives.
- If the script warns that the copied build is the base's, run `ant compileAll`, then the library order. Without the warning, `ant compileAll` keeps the seeded caches.
- If another agent seeded your worktree, make the script's two lists yourself: `git diff --name-only <base> -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` for the library sources, and `git diff --name-only <base> -- ProjectFortress/src ProjectFortress/astgen build.xml` for the warning.
- Reuse another tree's build or caches only through this script.

## Running the old code

If your worktree holds an edit and you need the base's behaviour, run the old code instead of reverting your edit. For example, see a test fail, or compare a program's old and new output.

`old-fortress.sh` runs the base build's `bin/fortress`. It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the base build and `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the private caches folder that you name, over your settings. Name a folder inside your worktree's `tmp/`:

    OLD=explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss     # the compiled path ...
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches run P             # ... then the run
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss             # walk
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches junit <worktree>/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/X.test [Y.test ...]   # compiled .test files, in one JVM

- Any copy of the tool works, because it runs the base build that its first argument names.
- On first use, it fills the private folder with a copy of the base build's caches (36 MB, 0.04 s). Later runs use the same folder.
- Every cache file that a run writes goes to the private folder, and nothing else that it writes under the base build stays. So several agents can run the old code at once.
- Keep your programs outside the base build too, because a program writes its own logs beside it. The tool refuses a private folder inside the base build (exit 2).

To run interpreter tests on the old code, run the base build's `harness-one.sh` with `FORTRESS_HOME` set to the base build:

    FORTRESS_HOME=<base-build> <base-build>/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh \
        <worktree>/tmp/old-harness <worktree>/ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss

The `run` step of a compiled `.test` is a separate `bin/fortress run` process. It inherits `FORTRESS_HOME` and `FORTRESS_CACHES`, and takes its class path from `FORTRESS_CACHES`. If you compose a harness run by hand with `-Dfortress.caches=<folder>`, set `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the same folder. Otherwise the `run` step fails with "Could not load ... Resource not found".

14	
15	## 1. In short
16	
17	- **The cause is the implementation, not a rule.** The Scala AST walker that ASTGen generates is one
18	  method. `Walker.walk` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala:1588-2023`)
19	  is a 216-case match: 213 node classes, then List, Option and anything else. It compiles to 31,704 bytes of
20	  bytecode.
21	  - HotSpot does not compile a method longer than its huge-method limit (8,000 bytes, while
22	    `DontCompileHugeMethods` is true, its default). So the method always runs in the interpreter.
23	  - Every type substitution, normalization, self-type removal and static-parameter clearing in the checker
24	    goes through it.
25	- **The fix.** `ScalaAstGenerator.java` emits the same cases in the same order, split into eight methods of
26	  30 cases each (`walkCases0` to `walkCases7`, the largest 4,474 bytes).
27	  - The regenerated `FortressAst.scala` differs only by the inserted method boundaries.
28	  - No switch.

30	  - 911 s before and 352 s after, a pair on the real build of the fix (F0, F1).

173	## 3. Rung C and the repair's bodies (item 2)
174	
175	Each variant was taken out in the shadow. All runs are instrumented and idle.
176	
177	| run | stage | apis | component | table |
178	|---|---|---|---|---|
179	| I5: repair in | 935 s | 293.8 s | 620.1 s | 39 / 38 / none |
180	| I4: rung C out | 826 s | 251.6 s | 554.3 s | 40 / 39, plus `:2623`, row 686's site, which rung C repaired |
181	| I6: repair out | 668 s | 298.5 s | 331 s, then the crash | 1 / 0, the crash at `:3059` |
182	| I7: the fix | 339 s | 68.0 s | 263.0 s | equal to I5 |
183	| I8: the fix, rung C out | 274 s | 60.9 s | 205.0 s | equal to I4 |
184	| I9: the JVM switch, no fix | 652 s | 92.0 s | 528.9 s | equal to I5 |
185	
186	**The repair: +267 s.** In order of checking, the component has 229 declarations before Array3:
187	
188	| run | the 229 before Array3 | Array3 | the 257 after Array3 |
189	|---|---|---|---|

191	| I5 (repair in) | 310.0 s | 60.4 s | 224.2 s |

197	**Rung C: +109 s before the fix, +65 s after it.**
198	- In the apis: FortressLibrary's overloading check takes 167.9 s with rung C out and 208.0 s with it in
199	  (+24 %).

202	  review's +22 % for the distance stage's FortressLibrary (batch 15's review, section 1): a lead, not a
203	  measurement.

206	the walker takes the stage from 935 s to 339 s.

208	## 4. The fix
209	
210	- **`ScalaAstGenerator.java:625-650`.**
211	  - `walk(node)` calls `walkCases0(node)`.
212	  - The class cases are emitted in their old order, 30 to a method.
213	  - Each method but the last ends with `case _ => walkCases<k+1>(node)`.
214	  - The last ends with the old List, Option and default cases.
215	- **`FortressAst.scala`.** The generator's output, regenerated by `ant compileAll`.
216	  - The unedited generator reproduces the tracked file byte for byte.
217	  - The edited one writes the patched file.
218	  - Every other generated file is identical once ASTGen's timestamp line is masked, as the build masks it.
219	- **Method sizes after the fix** (bytes): `walkCases0` 2,215; `walkCases1` 3,373; `walkCases2` 4,099;
220	  `walkCases3` 4,072; `walkCases4` 4,186; `walkCases5` 4,378; `walkCases6` 4,474; `walkCases7` under 1,000.
221	- **Size of the patch:** 40 lines changed in the generator and 37 lines inserted in the generated file. The
222	  test file is new.
223	- **No switch.**
224	
225	## 5. Why every answer stays (item 4)
226	
227	The fix reads no rule differently, so the specification and the papers are not concerned.
228	
229	A Scala `match` tries its cases in order and takes the first that matches. The split keeps every case, its
230	pattern and its body text unchanged, and in the same order.
231	- A value that matches none of a method's cases goes to the next method's first case. That case is the one
232	  that followed in the old single match.
233	- The last method keeps the old List, Option and default cases, in their order.
234	- So for every value the same case is chosen and the same code runs.
235	- The case bodies call `walk`, which a subclass may override, exactly as before. `walk`'s signature is
236	  unchanged.
237	
238	The patch only inserts method boundaries between unchanged case lines. The audit (§7) checked this on every
239	branch of a full run.
240	
241	## 6. Measurements
242	
243	**Machine:** nproc=4; Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 2100.000 MHz; openjdk 25.0.4.1; `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`.
244	Nothing else of mine ran beside a timed run. A sampler recorded the load every minute, and the java process
245	count was 1 throughout. Two runs had brief light work of mine beside them: niced JFR reading during T1 and
246	scalac compiles during I5. Their highest 1-minute load was 1.79 and 1.95.
247	
248	| run | start UTC | load at start | seconds | what |
249	|---|---|---|---|---|
250	| T1 | 19:48:54 | 0.91 | 953 | count stage, repair in (stock stage, limit raised) |
251	| T2 | 20:04:47 | 1.04 | 332 | plus a split testing `Node` first (variant C, not taken) |
252	| T3 | 20:10:19 | 1.22 | 344 | plus the split in order (first form of the patch) |
253	| I5 | 20:16:40 | 0.89 | 935 | instrumented, repair in |
254	| I4 | 20:32:15 | 1.04 | 826 | rung C out |
255	| I6 | 20:46:01 | 1.07 | 668 | repair out |
256	| I7 | 20:57:09 | 1.07 | 339 | the fix |
257	| I8 | 21:02:48 | 1.09 | 274 | the fix, rung C out |
258	| I9 | 21:07:22 | 1.03 | 652 | `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods`, no fix |
259	| D1 | 21:18:23 | 1.62 | 2,375 | distance stage, repair in (FortressLibrary 1,336, RangeInternals 762) |
260	| D2 | 21:58:01 | 1.03 | 931 | distance stage, repair and fix (FortressLibrary 462, RangeInternals 381) |
261	| F0 | 22:45:39 | 1.53 | 911 | final build, old walker first on the classpath, repair in a shadow |
262	| F1 | 23:00:50 | 1.02 | 352 | final build (the fix), repair in a shadow |
263	
264	**Answers, run against run.**
265	- **The count stage's table:** T1, T2, T3, I5, I7, I9, F0 and F1 give
266	  `#total 39`, `#locations 38`, `#crash none`, every api 0. That equals the cited idle run of 2026-10-14
267	  (`diff` prints nothing).
268	- **The checker's whole output:** T1 = T2 = F0 = F1, after masking the tree's path.
269	- **The distance stage:** D1 and D2 tables are equal but for `#seconds` and `#machine`. `errors.tsv` is
270	  identical (49 errors), and so is the whole output.
271	- **The repair on the distance stage:** D1 equals climb batch 15's landed `distance.txt` but for its crash
272	  row. With the repair in, the crash row goes (`#crash none`) and no site comes.
273	
274	## 7. The audit
275	
276	The audit variant of the walker checks, at every branch it takes, the index of that branch against the index
277	the original single match takes. The original's index is recomputed by its own tests in its order: equality
278	for the 15 stable identifiers, then the class tests, then List, Option, default.
279	
280	    @@AUDIT walk branches taken=279692861 mismatches=0 distinct-branches=90 of 216
281	
282	The audited run's table reads 38 / 37: row 488's `:130` is missing. The counting copies hash AST nodes. That
283	changes the JVM's identity-hash sequence, and with it the api order (§9). The JFR run (prof1) lost `:130` the
284	same way. Neither run's walker is the patch's.
285	
286	## 8. The tests
287	
288	`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/WalkerJUTest.java` is in the misc track and has four
289	tests:
290	
291	- `testEveryMethodCompilable`: every method of `Walker` is at most 8,000 bytes of bytecode, read with
292	  `java.lang.classfile`.
293	- `testIdentityWalkRebuildsNodes`: walked types are equal to the original and are new objects.
294	- `testOtherValuesComeBackAsTheyAre`: a String, a Span, an Integer, a `KindOp` node, None and Nil come back as
295	  the same objects.
296	- `testOverrideReachesNestedNodes`: an override reaches type variables nested in static arguments, tuples,
297	  arrows, intersections, unions, Options and Lists.
298	
299	**The runs.**
300	- On the base build's classes (2026-10-14 22:15 UTC):
301	
302	      java -cp <test classes>:<base build classpath> junit.textui.TestRunner com.sun.fortress.scala_src.nodes.WalkerJUTest
303	      .F...
304	      1) testEveryMethodCompilable(...)junit.framework.AssertionFailedError: Walker.walk is 31704 bytes of bytecode, more than 8000
305	      Tests run: 4,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0
306	
307	- With the fix built: `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=WalkerJUTest` gives "Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0",
308	  BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
309	- The test was written after the shadow prototypes, as a probe's is. Its failing run is on the base build.
310	- It is in Java because scalac 2.13 cannot read `java.lang.classfile`: "illegal cyclic reference involving
311	  class CodeImpl".
312	
313	**The suites, with the fix built and without the repair:**
314	- `ant testQuick`:
315	  - compiler 1,212, library 86, othercompiler 263, all with 0 failures;
316	  - BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 4 min 34 s.
317	- `ant testFast`:
318	  - 1,988 tests, 0 failures, BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 5 min 0 s;
319	  - misc track: 427 tests, the landed gate's 423 plus these 4.
320	- `ant testSystem`:
321	  - 149 + 150 + 161 + 161 = 621 tests, 0 failures;
322	  - 2 min 16 s.
323	
324	The counts equal climb batch 15's gate. The walker is shared by both paths' phases (the disambiguator, the
325	desugarers), hence `testSystem`.
326	
327	## 9. Row 488: the checker's output depends on identity hashes
328	
329	Every ASTGen node's `generateHashCode` starts from `getClass().hashCode()`, the `Class` object's identity
330	hash (for example `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TraitType.java:104`; 936 node classes do this).
331	
332	So the order of every `HashMap` and `HashSet` of nodes depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence. That
333	includes the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` iterates (`StaticChecker.java:125`). The sequence moves
334	whenever any code asks for an identity hash at a different moment.
335	
336	**The runs.** The fixed checker ran with a copy of the stage's driver that first asks for N identity hashes
337	(`-Dprobe.hashes=N`):
338	
339	| run | N | api check order | table | output |
340	|---|---|---|---|---|
341	| H0 | 0 | the usual one | 39 / 38 | identical to T1's |
342	| H1 | 1 | wholly different, starting RangeInternals, FortressLibrary, NativeArray | 39 / 38 | three messages print a union's members the other way |
343	| H2 | 1000 | another order | 39 / 38 | one message differs the same way |
344	
345	The messages that changed in H1:
346	- `:1463`: `OR(O0,I0)` became `OR(I0,O0)`.
347	- `:3367`: `OR(T,IntLiteral)` became `OR(IntLiteral,T)`.
348	- `:3384`: `OR(T,IntLiteral)` became `OR(IntLiteral,T)`.
349	
350	The two instrumented runs that hash nodes or add threads (JFR, the counts) lost `:130`.
351	
352	This is a lead for row 488's "mechanism unknown". The fix asks for no identity hash, which is why its outputs
353	are identical.
354	
355	## 10. What a landing would carry (item 5)
356	
357	- **`fix.patch`, applied and built with `ant compileAll`.** The build regenerates `FortressAst.scala` from the
358	  generator and reproduces the patch's file, so the two stay in step.
359	- **`WalkerJUTest`.** Its failing and passing runs are in §8.
360	- **No switch.**
361	- **With row 680's line in the same tree**, the count stage takes 352 s idle (F1), with the table above: 39
362	  errors, 38 locations, no crash.
363	  - About 447 s with the 27 % allowance for load, inside the 690 s of `CLIMB-BATCH-15.md:154`.
364	  - The repair's own landing promotes `XXXLocalFunctionSiblingInLoop` and `XXXLocalFunctionSiblingCall` and
365	    re-keys the recursive case to 'reference cycle', as `e75bb538b` says.
366	- **The distance stage** with both: 931 s and 49 errors, the crash row gone.
367	- **The gate.** The fix touches a walker that both paths' phases use, so its suites are the whole gate.
368	  - My `testFast` and `testSystem` runs were on the fix alone.
369	  - The repair adds its three test changes.
370	
371	## 11. Decisions, findings, questions
372	
373	**Decisions.** No decision of the curator covers 1 to 6.
374	
375	1. **The split in order (variant B).** Rejected:
376	   - variant C, which tests `Node` first and skips 213 tests for leaves: 332 s against B's 344 s, one run
377	     each, within noise; its exactness needs a proof (every node class implements `Node`);
378	   - the JVM switch alone: 652 s, and a switch every JVM would need;
379	   - a class-keyed dispatch.
380	2. **30 cases per method.** The largest method is 4,474 bytes, against the limit of 8,000.
381	3. **The patch changes the generator and the file it writes, not the file alone.** A build would otherwise
382	   regenerate the old walker the next time `Fortress.ast` or a generator changes.
383	4. **An audit by branch index, not by memo hits.** The fix adds no memo.
384	5. **The test is in Java**, because of the scalac 2.13 limit (§8).
385	6. **The brief's "distance stage is `tools/count-run/`" read as `tools/distance/run.sh`.** `count-run.sh`
386	   runs each interpreter test under walk.
387	
388	**Findings.**
389	- The interpreted walker (§2.2).
390	- The shares of the repair (+267 s) and of rung C (+109 s before the fix, +65 s after) (§3).
391	- After the fix, about 95 % of the component's time is in the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3).
392	- The checker's output depends on identity hashes (§9).
393	- The repair removes the distance stage's crash row and adds no site (§6).
394	- The other methods over the limit are negligible after the fix (§2.2).
395	
396	**Defects.**
397	- **The interpreted walker.** My change repairs it (way 1), pinned by `WalkerJUTest`. No ledger row holds it;
398	  the row to write:
399	  - claim: the generated `Walker.walk` (`FortressAst.scala`, from `ScalaAstGenerator.java`) is 31,704 bytes
400	    of bytecode, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte huge-method limit, so the JVM never compiles it, and every phase
401	    that walks a tree runs it in the interpreter;
402	  - status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, closed by the fix's commit;
403	  - class: implementation gap (generator, speed);
404	  - spec: silent;
405	  - reproducer: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`;
406	  - found by: this probe.
407	- **The identity-hash dependence.** A note for row 488, with the H runs' commands and outputs (§9).
408	
409	**Sentences of the specification made false:** none.
410	
411	**For FACTS.**
412	1. **The fact.** The generated AST walker's `walk` was one method over HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit, so it ran
413	   interpreted. With it split in order, the count stage with row 680's repair takes 352 s instead of 911 s,
414	   and the distance stage 931 s instead of 2,375 s, with identical output.
415	   - What it means: row 680's line can land under the 690 s rule.
416	   - Test: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`.
417	   - Detail: §2.2 and §6.
418	2. **The fact.** The checker's output depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence, because AST hashes include
419	   the `Class` identity hash. One extra identity hash at start reorders the api checks and the members of
420	   unions in messages.
421	   - What it means: the stages' outputs can move with an unrelated edit (row 488).
422	   - Command: the driver with `-Dprobe.hashes=1`.
423	   - Detail: §9.
424	3. **The fact.** Rung C's normal form costs 12 % of the count stage before the fix, 19 % after.
425	   - Detail: §3.
426	
427	**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
428	- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
429	- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
430	  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
431	- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
432	  message text, once.
433	
434	**Commands worked out.**
435	- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
436	  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
437	  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
438	- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
439	  longer than 8,000 bytes.
440	- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
441	  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
442	  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
443	  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
444	- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.
445	- **Moving the identity-hash sequence:** a driver copy that calls `new Object().hashCode()` N times before
446	  the phases.

<!-- The skeptic's review of fix.patch (the generated walker split into eight methods, with WalkerJUTest), by reading the patch and the code on main at 558ae0a10, rebuilding it in a worktree of its own, and timing one run of the count stage with row 680's repair on an idle machine. -->

# Skeptic's review: the generated walker split in order

## Verdict

**Approved.** No fixes, so there is no `fix-2.patch`.

- By reading, the split cannot change a result.
- The build regenerates the patch's file byte for byte.
- The test fails on main and passes with the fix.
- One idle run of the count stage, with the fix and row 680's repair, took **333 s**. Its whole output is identical to the idle run without the fix (959 s).

## 1. The results stay the same, by reading

- **The generated file only gains lines.** `git diff --numstat` on `FortressAst.scala` gives 37 lines added and 1 removed. The removed line is `def walk(node:Any):Any = {`. The added lines are:
  - `walk` delegating to `walkCases0`, at patched 1590-1591;
  - seven boundaries of 5 lines each, at 1653-1657, 1718-1722, 1783-1787, 1848-1852, 1913-1917, 1978-1982 and 2043-2047. Each boundary is `case _ => walkCases<k+1>(node)`, then the closing of one method and the opening of the next.
- **Every case keeps its pattern, its body and its place.** A diff made only of insertions cannot move or change a line.
  - The sizes are 30 class cases in each of `walkCases0` to `walkCases6`, and 3 in `walkCases7`, which is 213.
  - `walkCases7` then keeps `List`, `Option` and `case _ => node`, in their old order.
- **The generator** (`ScalaAstGenerator.java`, patched 625-670) builds the same `cases` list in the same order as before: `cList` reversed, ignored and abstract classes skipped.
  - The chunk loop never emits an empty method. When the count is a multiple of 30, the last full method gets the closing cases. With zero cases, `walkCases0` gets them.
  - The only `case _` before the last method is each method's own last case, which hands the value on to the next method.
- **No guards.** None of the 216 cases has an `if`.
- **Scala reads the patterns the same way in every method.** Each method has the same scope as the old `walk`, inside the same trait: `S*` stable identifiers and extractors at package level, and lower-case binders.
- **The order among class cases cannot matter at all.** I checked this with reflection over the built classes:
  - No case's class is a supertype of another's (0 pairs).
  - None of the 213 is abstract, and all 213 implement `Node`.
  - So at most one class case matches any value.
  - The 15 stable-identifier cases (`case SKindOp =>`, `FortressAst.scala:807-812`) compare by the extractor object's default `equals`, so they match no node.
  - Only "class cases before List, Option and the default" is order-sensitive, and that is kept.
- **Subclasses.** About 45 Scala subclasses extend `Walker`, per the grep. Many override `walk` and call `super.walk`. `walk` keeps its name and signature, and the case bodies still call the virtual `walk`.
  - No source defines a `walkCases*` member: grep over the whole repository, `tmp/` aside.
  - Scala would refuse an override without `override` anyway.
  - No user of `Walker` exists outside `ProjectFortress/src`.
  - No code or test inspects `Walker` stack frames. `FileTests.java:873` looks only for `Driver.evalComponent`.
- **Stack.** The old `walk` had `max_locals` 1,079. The new methods have 82 to 180 each, 1,107 summed over the whole chain. So an interpreted walk of a List, Option or String needs about the old frame's room plus small forwarder frames, and earlier node classes need far less.

## 2. The build makes the patch's file

**Setup.** No base build existed, since the probe's at 473ab6a30 was gone. So I built one at main's head 558ae0a10: `ant compileAll`, the library order and the BooleanOps walk run, then `git status` clean. I seeded `/home/user/fortress-sk16` from it.

**What I did.**
1. Applied `fix.patch` with `git apply`, which was clean.
2. Saved the patched `FortressAst.scala`, then put main's version back, so that the build had to regenerate it.
3. Ran `ant compileAll`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 40 s.
   - It printed `Processing .../Fortress.ast`.
   - `makeAST` ran because the generator's source was newer than `Library/FortressAst.fsi` (`build.xml:644-646`).

**What I found.**
- The regenerated `FortressAst.scala` is byte-identical to the patch's (`cmp`).
- The tree's whole diff, with the test file added, equals `fix.patch` except for its `index` lines.
- No other generated file changed: not `nodes/`, not `Library/FortressAst.fs*`.
- The base build also ran `makeAST` with the unedited generator and stayed clean. So the old generator reproduces main's file.

## 3. The test

**Fails on main.** I compiled `WalkerJUTest` against the base build's classes. `junit.textui.TestRunner` gave "Tests run: 4, Failures: 1": `testEveryMethodCompilable` fails with "Walker.walk is 31704 bytes of bytecode, more than 8000".

**Passes with the fix.** `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=WalkerJUTest` gives "Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0", BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

**It runs in the misc track.** The track includes `**/*JUTest.class` (`build.xml:1200`). On a clean build:
- scalac runs first and parses the Java sources for their signatures (`build.xml:753-783`);
- javac then compiles the test against the built `Walker` (`build.xml:785` onward).

**What it catches.**
- A later `Fortress.ast` change makes the build regenerate the walker. The size test reads the built `Walker.class` and fails on any method of `Walker` over 8,000 bytes, naming the method and its size.
- The margin is wide. The largest method is 4,474 bytes (about 149 bytes per case). A 30-case chunk would need about 267 bytes per case to pass the limit.
- It also catches a generator that goes back to one method.
- The behaviour tests catch a broken chain anywhere in `walkCases0` to `walkCases6`. List and Option sit in the last method, so with a broken chain `testOverrideReachesNestedNodes` would get them back unwalked.

**What it misses.**
1. Methods over the limit outside `Walker` (section 5).
2. A JIT bail-out on a method under the limit. Size is necessary for compilation, not sufficient.
3. A single dropped case of a node class that the tests do not sample. Only a handful of type nodes and `TypeArg` are walked.
4. Speculation churn. I ran `-XX:+PrintCompilation` for 150 s on the same stage:
   - All eight methods compiled at tiers 2, 3 and 4, with no `COMPILE SKIPPED`.
   - There were 80 "made not entrant: uncommon trap" recompiles. The last of them came at 88 s.

It guards the right thing for this defect.

## 4. The time and the results, measured once

**Tree.** The fix plus row 680's line (`Decls.scala:414`, `makeTryChecker(this)` to `makeTryChecker(newChecker)`), built with `ant compileAll`: 26 s, scalac recompiled everything.

**Stage.** A copy of `run.sh` in my `tmp/`, whose only change is `timeout -k 10 900` to `3000`.

**Machine.**
- nproc 4, Xeon at 2.10 GHz.
- Before the start: no java process. I waited until the 1-minute load was under 1.0.
- During the run: only the stage's java process and its `timeout` wrapper.
- Load sampled each minute: 0.98 at the start, then 1.14, 1.31, 1.11, 1.04, 1.05, and 1.02 at the end.

**Run.** 23:29:57 to 23:35:30 UTC: **333 s**, the whole `run.sh`, its javac included.

| run | seconds |
|---|---|
| this run (fix and repair) | 333 |
| probe's F1 (fix and repair) | 352 |
| probe's F0 (repair, no fix) | 911 |
| idle measure without the fix, at 994dc944c | 959 |

994dc944c has the same code as 558ae0a10: `git diff` of `ProjectFortress`, `Library`, `build.xml`, `bin` and the stage is empty. This run is well inside the 690 s rule of `CLIMB-BATCH-15.md:154`.

**Results.**
- The table equals `measure-680-run1-table.txt`: `#total 39`, `#locations 38`, `#crash none`, every api 0, `#shadow` matching.
- The whole checker output, 178 lines, equals `measure-680-run1-full-output.txt` once `/home/user/fortress-m680` and `/home/user/fortress-sk16` are masked. That includes the last line `### rc=-1`. The output holds no time lines.
- So under P-148 the checker accepts and refuses the same programs, with the same errors at the same places.

## 5. What else the landing must carry

**Must carry:**
- `fix.patch` as it stands. It applies cleanly to 558ae0a10.
- Row 680's line, with its own test changes (`e75bb538b`).
- The gate's suites, both of them: the walker is used by phases of both paths.
- The ledger row and the FACTS entries that the probe proposes (`REPORT.md` §11).

**Other generated walkers.** No method generated from `Fortress.ast` is near the limit after the fix. I scanned `ProjectFortress/build` with `java.lang.classfile` for methods of 5,000 bytes or more. The in-repo generators' Java visitors have one small method per class.

**Methods over or near the limit.** None needs to be in this landing. The probe measured them at 9 of 14,819 samples after the fix. They are candidates for a later pass:
- `NodeReader.readNode`, 14,026 bytes: a chain of 938 string comparisons that ASTGen's own serializer generates (`astgen.jar`, `generateSerializers yes`). It runs on every AST cache read (`ASTIO.java:150`).
- `Misc.checkExprMisc`, 12,893.
- `HygienicRenamer.walk`, 11,599.
- `ExprDisambiguator.walk`, 8,518: 6.5 % over, and both paths' disambiguation runs it.
- The Rats! parsers' `pCharLiteralContent$1`, 23,717, three copies.
- The parsers' `pidrest`, 7,617, four copies: 95 % of the limit.

## Fixes

None.

## For the curator

1. **Land it.** The stage with both the fix and the repair took 352 s (F1) and 333 s (this run), against 959 s without the fix, with identical output.
2. **Q1 of the report** (with the repair or ahead of it) is still yours. Nothing here prefers one or the other: the split changes no result either way.
3. **A wider guard is a decision not taken.** One test could scan the whole build for methods over 8,000 bytes, with an allow-list of today's six. It would catch the hand-written ones and any new one. It is not needed for this landing.
4. **A nit, not fixed.** The generator joins each case's two lines with a literal `"\n"` inside a `println` (patched `ScalaAstGenerator.java:646-647`, `:654`). The output is identical on Linux. Only a Windows build would mix line endings.
5. **Scratch.** The outputs of this review are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/sk16/`:
   - `skeptic-run-full-output.txt`, `skeptic-run-table.txt`, `skeptic-run-log.txt` and `skeptic-run-load.txt`;
   - `skeptic-printcompilation-walker.txt`;
   - `sizes-base.txt`;
   - the checking programs `MethodSizes.java` and `SubCheck.java`.

   Both worktrees (`/home/user/fortress-skb`, `/home/user/fortress-sk16`) are removed. Nothing is committed or pushed.

369 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15/RECORD.md
# Climb batch 15: the gather's record

Written at the gather stage of climb batch 15 (2026-10-14), the run of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-15.md` (rungs B, C, L and O), on `main` from the base `ee1aa1a95524ad9c3952462f665632deff844bbb`. `main` was at `6a3e20783` when the gather began, sixteen coordinator commits above the base, which touch only `.claude/skills/coordinator/`, `explorations/coordinator/` (`BOOT.md`, `FACTS.md`, `FACTS-history.md`, `HELD.md`, `INDEX.md`, `process-engineering/plan-map.md`) and `explorations/reviews/astra-record-keeping-review.md`, no file a rung touches (`git diff --stat ee1aa1a95 6a3e20783`). All four rungs were approved, none after a judge's ruling and none with a repair round, and each landed as one commit composed from its branch's net change; no branch is a parent of anything on `main`, and each branch stays as it is.

**Preconditions.** `git status --porcelain` was empty, and `ee1aa1a95` is an ancestor of `HEAD` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, exit 0).

**Scratch.** The patches are `tmp/gather/<slug>.patch` in the main tree, each `git diff ee1aa1a95...<branch>`. One tree was seeded outside the main tree from the batch's base build, with `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base15 /home/user/fortress-gather15 - ee1aa1a95524ad9c3952462f665632deff844bbb` ("seeded from /home/user/fortress-base15 (ee1aa1a95) in 3 s"); nothing was built or run in the main tree or in the base build. In `/home/user/fortress-gather15` the four patches were applied in the order below with `git apply --3way --index` (no conflict), then `ant compileAll` ("Caches /home/user/fortress-gather15/default_repository/caches started again, empty", "BUILD SUCCESSFUL", "Total time: 51 seconds") and the library order (five compiles, each `rc=0`, five jars). The closing tests ran there. After the closes, `git diff --cached --stat 59b1d0a4d -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml` in that tree printed only `Library/FortressLibrary.fss | 4 ++--`, the gather's respelling of `additiveIdentity`'s doc comment on the same lines (rung L, below); so the code and tests the tests ran on are `59b1d0a4d`'s but for a comment. In `Specification/` the two trees differ only by the row numbers the gather put in place of the placeholders.

## The landed commits

| Order | Rung | Branch | Commit on `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C, `rung-checker-bounds` | `wip/rung-checker-bounds` at `7d388760b` | `f237148ac` |
| 2 | B, `rung-walk-elements` | `wip/rung-walk-elements` at `193199afe` | `20474c144` |
| 3 | L, `rung-library-factories` | `wip/rung-library-factories` at `496ba5615` | `a0f839ad7` |
| 4 | O, `rung-duplicates-coverage` | `wip/rung-duplicates-coverage` at `93f579495` | `59b1d0a4d` |
| | the rows' closes | | `32af87b18` |

## The order the rungs were applied in

C, then B, then L, then O, read from `git diff -U0 ee1aa1a95...<branch>`.
- The shared files are three: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` (B and L), `Library/IntMap.fss` (B and L) and `Specification/appendices/changes.tex` (B, L and O). C shares no file with any rung: its checker file, `TypeAnalyzer.scala`, and its tests are its own.
- The lowest edited line of each rung in those files, on the base: B `FortressLibrary.fss:1314`, `IntMap.fss:732`, `changes.tex:1032`; L `FortressLibrary.fss:2451`, `IntMap.fss:520`, `changes.tex:2401`; O `changes.tex:2500`.
- File by file, `FortressLibrary.fss` gives B before L, `changes.tex` gives B, L, O, and `IntMap.fss` gives L before B. Taken as one number per rung, the rule gives L (`:520`), B (`:732`), O (`:2500`).
- The gather took B, L, O, the order of the two files that both B and L shift. The rule's purpose is that a later hunk not shift what a landed record cites. B's 121 net lines at `FortressLibrary.fss:1318` and its 112 net lines in `changes.tex` from `:1033` would move every line of L's array factories and of L's and O's `changes.tex` entries if they landed later; under the order taken no hunk lands above an earlier rung's line in those two files but one: O's Effect sentences on row 707, 5 net lines at O's `changes.tex:2500`, land above L's Original text in the same entry, `:2567-2571` on L's tree, `:2684-2688` on `main` (the merged-diff review). In `IntMap.fss` both rungs replace one line by one line (`:520` and `:732`), so neither moves the other's lines whichever goes first.
- C, which shares no file, went first, as batch 14's gather placed its rung with no shared file; it moves no other rung's line, and no other rung edits its files.
