The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes
        write_text(p.ledger, led.text())
    print('row %d, in "%s"' % (num, sec.title))
    files = backtick_paths(line)
    kin = sorted({r.num for r in led.rows if r.num != num for f in files if cites(r.line, f)})
    if kin:
        print('rows that cite the same files: %s' % ', '.join(map(str, kin[:20])) + (' and %d more' % (len(kin) - 20) if len(kin) > 20 else ''))


def cmd_note(a, p):
    text = escape_pipes(one_line(a.text))
    if not text:
        raise LedgerError('note needs a TEXT')
    with Lock(p.lock):
        led = Ledger(p.ledger)
        r = led.one(a.n)
        if r.status_word in ('FIXED', 'DUPLICATE'):
            raise LedgerError('row %d is %s: a closed row is not edited; its full text is in the history file' % (r.num, r.status_word))
        cells = r.template_cells()
        cells[7] = (cells[7] + ' ' + text).strip()
        line = join_cells(cells)
        template_row(line, {x.num for x in led.rows}, p.root)
        replace_rows(p, led, [(r, line, 'note added')])
    print('row %d: note added (%d characters)' % (r.num, len(line)))


def cmd_close(a, p):
    root = p.root
    if git(root, 'rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', a.commit + '^{commit}').returncode != 0:
        raise LedgerError('%s is not a commit' % a.commit)
    if git(root, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', a.commit, 'HEAD').returncode != 0:
        raise LedgerError('%s is not in the history of HEAD: close a row after its fix has landed' % a.commit)
    short = git(root, 'rev-parse', '--short=9', a.commit).stdout.strip()
    with Lock(p.lock):
        led = Ledger(p.ledger)
        r = led.one(a.n)
        lint = Linter(root, {x.num for x in led.rows})
        test = lint.test_path(a.test)
        if r.status_word in ('FIXED', 'DUPLICATE'):
            raise LedgerError('row %d is already closed (%s)' % (r.num, r.status_word))
        if r.status_word in ('RETIRED', 'CONTESTED'):
            raise LedgerError('row %d is %s, which is not a defect to close' % (r.num, r.status_word))
        notes = 'fixed `%s`' % short + ('; ' + escape_pipes(one_line(a.note)) if a.note else '') + '; full text: history, row %d' % r.num
        cells = [str(r.num), pick(a.claim, first_sentence(r.claim)), 'FIXED', pick(a.klass, r.klass),
                 pick(a.spec, r.spec), '`%s`' % test, pick(a.found_by, r.found_by), notes]
        line = join_cells(cells)
        template_row(line, {x.num for x in led.rows}, root)
        replace_rows(p, led, [(r, line, 'closed by %s' % short)])
    print('row %d: FIXED by %s, test %s; its earlier line is in %s' % (r.num, short, test, os.path.basename(p.history)))


def cmd_duplicate(a, p):
    if a.n == a.of:
        raise LedgerError('a row is not a duplicate of itself')
    with Lock(p.lock):
        led = Ledger(p.ledger)
        r, other = led.one(a.n), led.one(a.of)
        if r.status_word == 'DUPLICATE':
            raise LedgerError('row %d is already a duplicate' % r.num)
        if other.status_word == 'DUPLICATE':
            raise LedgerError('row %d is itself a duplicate: point at the row it names' % other.num)
        numbers = {x.num for x in led.rows}
        cells = [str(r.num), pick(a.claim, first_sentence(r.claim)), 'DUPLICATE', pick(a.klass, r.klass),
                 pick(a.spec, r.spec), pick(a.reproducer, r.reproducer), pick(a.found_by, r.found_by),
                 'duplicate of row %d; full text: history, row %d' % (other.num, r.num)]
        line = join_cells(cells)
        template_row(line, numbers, p.root)
        changes = [(r, line, 'duplicate of row %d' % other.num)]
        if a.add:
            oc = other.template_cells()
            oc[7] = (oc[7] + ' ' + escape_pipes(one_line(a.add))).strip()
            oline = join_cells(oc)
            template_row(oline, numbers, p.root)
            changes.append((other, oline, 'note added from row %d, now its duplicate' % r.num))
        replace_rows(p, led, changes)
    print('row %d: DUPLICATE of row %d%s; earlier lines in %s' % (
        r.num, other.num, ', and row %d\'s notes extended' % other.num if a.add else '', os.path.basename(p.history)))


def pick(given, old):
    return escape_pipes(one_line(given)) if given is not None else old


def cmd_check(a, p):
    if a.rows:
        rows, other = rows_file(a.rows)
        numbers = {r.num for r in rows if r.num is not None}
        if os.path.exists(p.ledger):
            numbers |= {r.num for r in Ledger(p.ledger).rows}
        lint = Linter(p.root, numbers)
        fails = [(None, 'not-a-row', 'line %d: %s' % (i, clip(ln, 60))) for i, ln in other]
        seen = collections.Counter(r.num for r in rows if r.num is not None)
        fails += [(None, 'number', 'row %d is on %d lines of %s' % (n, k, a.rows)) for n, k in sorted(seen.items()) if k > 1]
        for r in rows:
            fails += [(r, rule, d) for rule, d in lint.lint(r)]
        name, total = a.rows, len(rows)
    else:
        led = Ledger(p.ledger)
        fails = Linter(p.root, {r.num for r in led.rows}).lint_ledger(led)
        name, total = os.path.basename(p.ledger), len(led.rows)
        if a.base:
            fails += check_base(a.base, led, p)
    rows_failing = set()
    by_rule = collections.Counter()
    seen = set()
    for r, rule, d in fails:
        key = (id(r) if r is not None else d, rule)
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            by_rule[rule] += 1
        if r is not None:
            rows_failing.add(id(r))

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

## 1. What changed, and why

The base is ee1aa1a95. The branch holds one edit of the checker, in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`, from the checker probe's two patches (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-bound-defects/patches/rows-686-687-689-690-normal-form.patch` and `sibling-ground-bound.patch`), applied unchanged (`4356454a2`):

- **The normal form** (`normConjunct`, `TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-735`). A closed trait among the conjuncts of an intersection is replaced by the types its `comprises` clause lists that another conjunct excludes only where that conjunct names no type variable and no inference variable (`excludedListed`, `:713-714`). A bound such as `K ∩ R[\T\]` therefore stays the intersection as written, the redundancy branch drops `K` beside a `T` whose bound implies it, and no union the checker builds over such a bound holds a variable. This is the condition under which the POPL 2019 paper proves matching complete (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, section 6), the type group's late word (P-26). Before the edit, `K ∩ R[\$T\]` became `OR(AND(A,R[$T]),AND(B,R[$T]))`, and the union rule split it before the variable's bound was read (the probe's section 2.2). One change clears rows 686, 687, 689 and 690.
- **The union cases** (`pSubInner`, `TypeAnalyzer.scala:165-180`, before the union rule at `:181-182`, both only where the check is not negated). An inference variable below a union takes the union as one upper bound (`:168`), so the inference-variable rule of `fig-subtype.tick` comes before its union rule. A type variable below a union is also tried through its bound, with the type-variable case's history entry (`:171-180`). This clears the ground sibling (711): `g[\T extends { K, Q }\](x: T): T = h(x)` with `trait Q excludes { C }`, where `K ∩ Q` is ground and still expanded to `OR(A,B)`. The solver then takes the intersection of the upper bounds, here the union, which is the bound: P-48.

Row 680's line (`row-680-local-function-group.patch`, `makeTryChecker(this)` to `makeTryChecker(newChecker)` in the `SLetFn` case, `impls/Decls.scala:414`) was applied, built and tested (`3216343f6`), and then held (`e75bb538b`). With it, and with `__bigOperator`'s `body(i)` typed for one run only, the count stage checked the library component whole and took 809 s, past the 690 s that the batch record sets for landing it (section 6). The line is valid and its tests passed on it (section 2). Its tests stay in the tree as expected failures keyed on today's crashes.

## 2. The tests: the failing run and the passing run

All are in `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`. They were written first (`d7bf79b07`) and run through the harness on the base's code before the edit was first built:

- the four expected failures promoted, `git mv` without the prefix, each `compile`, `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`: `InferCallerTwoBoundsClosedTrait` (686), `CoerceTwoBoundsClosedTrait` (687), `CallerParamTwoBoundsClosedTrait` (689), `ReturnRuleTwoBoundsClosedTrait` (690);
- `CallerParamTwoGroundBoundsClosedTrait`, the sibling (`repro/BoundsGround.fss`), a plain run test asserting its two values;
- row 680's three: `LocalFunctionSiblingInLoop` and `LocalFunctionSiblingCall` (typecheck), from `repro/LocalSiblingInLoop.fss` and `LocalSiblingDirect.fss`, and `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn` (compile, keyed `reference cycle`), from `repro/LocalRecursiveUntyped.fss`;

The failing run was on the base's code at 2026-10-14T10:56:40Z, before the first build of the edit (`ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests <the 9 files and the 3 kept tests>`):

The 18 failures are the compile, link and run cases of the five run tests, the two typecheck tests and the recursive case. The recursive case failed with 'Saw wrong failure. compile', the base saying 'Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes'. `SelfTypeReturnSelfAtTraitRun` passed on the base ('cat', 'PASS'), as review-routed.1 asks. The kept `OverloadTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, `OverloadTwoBoundsClosedFamily` and `InferUnionInstanceArg` passed too.

With all three patches (later committed as `4356454a2` and `3216343f6`), the same list gave `OK (30 tests)` (11:00:27Z). (* A local function whose return type is left out and whose body calls a sibling local function of its block type checks when a loop body calls it, since the local functions of one block are mutually recursive (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations"). *)
component XXXLocalFunctionSiblingInLoop
export Executable

run(): () = do

    plane(k: ZZ32) = row(k) + row(k)
    for k <- 0#3 do

    end
    println("PASS")
  end

end

== XXXLocalFunctionSiblingCall.fss
(* A local function whose return type is left out and whose body calls a sibling local function of its block type checks when it is called, since the local functions of one block are mutually recursive (functions.tex, section "Local Function Declarations"). *)

export Executable

run(): () = do
    row(i: ZZ32) = i + 1
    plane(k: ZZ32) = row(k) + row(k)

(* A recursive local function that leaves its return type out stops the compiled checker, where a top-level function in a reference cycle gets the checker's refusal. *)
component XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn

run(): () = do
    fact(n: ZZ32) = if n = 0 then 1 else n fact(n - 1) end
    assert(fact(3), 6, "fact(3)")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

// The gate. Its steps and their reasons are the skill's gate.md, which this role follows; what
// stands here is what the skill points to the script for: the calls of the shell functions that
// write and compare the summary and the ladder (tools/gate-functions.sh, which a gate run by hand
// sources too), the atomic runs' lines in the summary, the checker count and the distance stage
// (the ladder's metrics, which the skill does not carry: POSITIONS.md, "The skills are written for
// a reader new to the repository ..."), testSpecData once a rung brings it, and the machine line.
// It commits nothing: the review commits in this tree beside it, and the commit stage lands its
// outputs.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const ATOMIC_OTHER = 'atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2'

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table was produced, 1 if it could not be. 20 s in the main tree,
# measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
set -u

STOCK_SHA=16e6e11df9341a67038b7d7cc9f0d7bb5e5a6149019f09e92545a8b646363a0b   # ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java, 2026-09-22

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count"
TARGET=Library/FortressLibrary.fss
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/checker-count.$$}
STOCK=$FH/ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java
OVERLOAD_CACHE=false     # the overloading checker's memo, off: see the header

mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "checker-count: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi

# The cloud container

**container**
: Virtual machine with its own disk, on which a cloud session of Claude Code runs. It holds a clone of the branch that the session was created from.

**curator**
: Person in charge of this restoration.

**main session**
: Top-level session of a container, which the curator talks to. The agents that it launches are not main sessions.

**coordinating session**
: Main session that keeps the project's files under `explorations/coordinator/` and launches the workers.

**process stop**
: End of the session's Claude Code process, by the platform's cap, by idleness or by a VM restart. The platform starts the process again in the same session.

**VM restart**
: Restart of the container's machine under a live session.

**check-in**
: One-shot reminder, armed with `send_later`, that wakes the main session with a message at a set time.

**Stop hook**
: Command that Claude Code runs at the end of every turn of the main session.

The platform stops the session's process about every 13 hours and when the session goes idle. It can restart the VM, sometimes with the disk rolled back, and it can lose the container. Running agents survive none of these.

## Rules for every agent

- Before a long run, read the room left on the disk as `references/machine.md` says.
- If your brief lets you push, push your work as you go, as `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md` says. Only what is pushed survives a rollback of the disk or a lost container.
- After a process stop, a VM restart or a lost container, run `git status` and `git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` in each tree that you work in, before you start anything again.
- The platform's git-check Stop hook asks the main session to commit and push. Treat its reminders as advisory. Never commit or push unready work to answer one.

## The parts

- `references/machine.md`, for every agent: the machine, timings across sessions, agents at once, the disk allowance and a full disk, the blocked hosts.
- `references/stops.md`, for every agent: the kinds of process stop and their signs, a disk rolled back, the weekly usage limit, what a stop keeps here. Its section on check-ins is for the coordinating session.
- `references/hooks.md`, for the coordinating session: the transcript backup and its blind spots, the git-check hook and how to turn it off.
- `references/container-loss.md`, for the coordinating session: re-provisioning, re-arming the backup, reading another session's transcript, recovering the work.

How a Claude Code session behaves anywhere (the Bash tool, long commands, waits and the prompt cache, interrupts, the automatic permission check) is `fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`. Running agents and resuming a run are the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`.

`references/sources.md` gives the source of each fact in these parts. Use it only to maintain this skill. Do not load it for a task.

# The machine and the network

## The machine

- 4 CPUs (Intel Xeon, at 2.1 or 2.8 GHz, which differs between sessions), about 15 GB of memory, and no swap. `nproc`, `free -g` and `/proc/cpuinfo` read them.
- Compare no absolute seconds across sessions: the same work has run 40 % slower in another session.
- A Workflow run starts at most two agents at a time on this machine. The others wait for a free slot. Two agents that build share the four cores.

## The disk allowance

`df -h /` misleads. Its Size column is the whole disk, about 250 GB, and most of it is reserved and cannot be written. The session may use Used plus Avail, about 37 GB, and Use% is taken of that sum. Read the Avail column: it is what is left.

- When the allowance is full, tool output fails with "no space left on device". Check Avail before a long run, and before you seed worktrees or copy builds.
- Temporary files that the work never deletes fill it. In this repository, they are mostly the parser's folders in `/tmp`. `fortress-repo`'s `references/build-and-caches.md` gives their sweep.
- When it is full, stop your own background processes (`fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`). Delete what you made and no longer need: scratch, build output, private caches, and finished worktrees whose commits are pushed.
- If that is not enough, commit and push, and report that this session's allowance is spent. A new session starts on a fresh machine.

## The network

Outbound HTTPS goes through the session's proxy, which blocks some hosts. `web.archive.org` resets the connection, and the proxy refuses `labs.oracle.com`.

- If you need a research PDF from these hosts, name it in your report. Only the curator can upload it into the session.
- To read an archived page that is not a PDF, fetch it through the pure.md reader relay: `https://pure.md/https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<url>`. The `if_` after the timestamp is required.

#!/bin/bash
# The full gate, once, on the main tree with the checker-speed fix and fork 2's library half applied
# (gate.md's steps, the workflow's gateRole and commit-stage outputs). Scratch: not committed.
cd /home/user/fortress && mkdir -p tmp
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH
export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD FORTRESS_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$PWD/tmp"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
source tmp/gate-functions.sh
L=tmp/gate-batch-13b ; O=$L/out
step () { echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" ; }

step "1 disk" ; df -h / | tail -1
rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS $L && mkdir -p $L $O

step "2 compileAll"
ant compileAll > $L/compileAll.txt 2>&1 ; echo "compileAll rc=$?"
grep -h 'Caches .*default_repository' $L/compileAll.txt

step "2b distance stage started in the background"
( explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh $O/distance.txt $L/distance > $L/distance.txt 2>&1 ; echo EXIT=$? >> $L/distance.txt ) &
DPID=$!

step "3 library order if the caches were emptied, then the ladder's two copies"
if grep -q 'default_repository/caches started again, empty' $L/compileAll.txt ; then
  ( cd ProjectFortress && for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
      echo "== $f" ; ../bin/fortress compile $f ; echo "rc=$?" ; done ; ls ../default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/ ) > $L/library.txt 2>&1
fi
ls default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/
D=$PWD/$L/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

step "4 testFast" ; ant testFast > $L/testFast.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testFast rc=$?"
step "4 testSystem" ; ant testSystem > $L/testSystem.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testSystem rc=$?"
step "4 testSpecData" ; ant testSpecData > $L/testSpecData.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testSpecData rc=$?"

step "5 summary and comparison"
gate_summary $L $O/summary.txt
LS=$(last_landed_summary) ; echo "last landed summary: $LS"
gate_compare "$LS" $O/summary.txt > $L/gate-compare.txt ; echo "gate_compare rc=$?" ; cat $L/gate-compare.txt

step "6 atomic runs"
( atomic_runs $O/summary.txt ) ; echo "atomic rc=$?"
grep '^# atomic' $O/summary.txt | grep -v PASS

step "7 ladder regression"
B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
    -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
    -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
    -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt
{ bash $D/run-subset.sh ; echo "run-subset rc=$?" ; python3 $D/classify.py ; echo "classify rc=$?" ;
  bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh ; echo "microgpt-phase.sh rc=$?" ; python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py ; echo "microgpt-phase.py rc=$?" ; } > $L/ladder.txt 2>&1
grep 'rc=' $L/ladder.txt
ladder_compare $B $D > $L/ladder-comparison.txt 2>&1
diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md) > $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt 2>&1
cat $L/ladder-comparison.txt $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt | sed 's/^/# ladder /' >> $O/summary.txt
mkdir -p $O/ladder
cp $D/ladder.tsv $D/microgpt-phase.md $O/ladder/
cp $L/ladder-comparison.txt $O/ladder/comparison.txt
cp $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt $O/ladder/microgpt-comparison.txt
echo "ladder lines:" ; cat $L/ladder-comparison.txt $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt

step "8 checker count"
CS=$(date +%s)
explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh $O/checker-count.txt $L/checker-count > $L/checker-count.txt 2>&1 ; echo "checker-count rc=$? secs=$(( $(date +%s) - CS ))"
LC=$(last_landed_checker_count) ; echo "last landed count: $LC"
checker_compare "$LC" $O/checker-count.txt "1" > $L/checker-compare.txt ; echo "checker_compare rc=$?"
sed 's/^/# checker /' $L/checker-compare.txt >> $O/summary.txt
cat $L/checker-compare.txt

step "10 microGPT quick walk checks"
explorations/coordinator/tools/mg-run.sh $L/microgpt-walk batch-13b > $L/microgpt-walk.txt 2>&1 ; echo "mg-run rc=$?"
grep -h "VERDICT\|^rc=" $L/microgpt-walk/*.txt

step "9 distance stage: wait"
wait $DPID
tail -3 $L/distance.txt
LD=$(git -C "$FORTRESS_HOME" log --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/distance.txt' 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/distance.txt' | grep -m1 'distance.txt$')
echo "last landed distance: $LD"
explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh "$LD" $O/distance.txt > $L/distance-compare.txt 2>&1
sed 's/^/# distance /' $L/distance-compare.txt >> $O/summary.txt
cat $L/distance-compare.txt
grep -h "VERDICT\|^rc=" $L/microgpt-walk/*.txt | sed 's/^/# microgpt-walk /' >> $O/summary.txt

step "done"

< # gate-functions.sh: the shell functions of the gate's summary and of its ladder comparison.
< #
< #   gate_summary <log-dir> <out-file> [machine-label]
< #                         writes summary.txt: one row per suite from the plain-formatter files under
< #                         $FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/, then the BUILD and Total time
< #                         lines of <log-dir>/{compileAll,testFast,testSystem,testSpecData}.txt, then
< #                         "# machine " lines from machine.sh with the label (default "gate")
< #   gate_compare <last-landed-summary> <this-summary>
< #                         prints the red lines (RED, EMPTY, COUNT DOWN, SUITE GONE), exit 1 if any;
< #                         the system-<i> rows are one suite split by sorted index, compared by their sum
< #   last_landed_summary   prints the path of the newest landed summary.txt
< #   ladder_filter <file>  masks the "Operation took" time of a ladder run's output
< #   ladder_compare <baseline-dir> <now-dir>
< #                         one DOWN, UP, NEW, MISSING or STDOUT line per ladder file that moved
< #   mg_phases <microgpt-phase.md>
< #                         one "component<TAB>phase" line per row of the microGPT phase table
< #
< # Source it from the tree's root, with FORTRESS_HOME set to that root, in the same Bash call that uses
< # the functions, since each call starts a new shell:
< #
< #     source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh
< #
< # It defines the functions and runs nothing. The batch script's gate role
< # (explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js, steps 5 and 7) sources it, and so can any gate run
< # by hand (the fortress-repo skill's gate.md). Until 2026-10-10 the functions were strings of the batch
< # script, and the skill extracted them with node and awk (explorations/reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md,
< # finding GA2).
< 
< gate_summary () {
<     local L="$1" O="$2" R="$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS" f
<     {
<       printf '#suite\ttests\tfailures\terrors\tskipped\n'
<       for f in "$R"/fast-*/TEST-*.txt "$R"/system-*/TEST-*.txt "$R"/TEST-*SpecDataJUTest.txt ; do
<         [ -f "$f" ] || continue
<         awk -v track="$(case "$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")" in TEST-RESULTS) echo specdata ;; *) basename "$(dirname "$f")" ;; esac)" -F'[ ,:]+' '
<           /^Testsuite:/ { n = split($2, p, "."); s = p[n] }
<           /^Tests run:/ { print track "/" s "\t" $3 "\t" $5 "\t" $7 "\t" $9 ; exit }' "$f"
<       done | sort
<       for f in compileAll testFast testSystem testSpecData ; do
<         [ -f "$L/$f.txt" ] && grep -h '^BUILD \|^Total time:' "$L/$f.txt" | sed "s|^|# $f: |"
<       done
<       bash explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/machine.sh "${3:-gate}" | sed 's|^|# machine |'
<     } > "$O"
< }
< 
< gate_compare () {
<     awk -F'\t' '
<       function key(s) { sub("^system-[0-9]+/", "system/", s) ; return s }
<       FNR == NR { if ($0 !~ /^#/ && NF == 5) base[key($1)] += $2 ; next }
<       $0 !~ /^#/ && NF == 5 {
<           k = key($1) ; seen[k] = 1 ; cur[k] += $2
<           if ($3 + 0 > 0 || $4 + 0 > 0)              { print "RED\t" $1 "\t" $3 " failures, " $4 " errors" ; bad++ }
<           if ($2 + 0 == 0)                           { print "EMPTY\t" $1 ; bad++ }
<       }
<       END { for (k in cur) if ((k in base) && cur[k] < base[k]) { print "COUNT DOWN\t" k "\t" base[k] " -> " cur[k] ; bad++ }
<             for (s in base) if (!(s in seen)) { print "SUITE GONE\t" s "\t" base[s] " -> absent" ; bad++ }
<             if (bad) exit 1 }' "$1" "$2"
< }
< 
< last_landed_summary () {
<     git -C "$FORTRESS_HOME" log --name-only --pretty=format: -- \
<         'explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/summary.txt' \
<         'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt' | grep -m1 'summary.txt$'
< }
< 
< ladder_filter () { sed -E 's/Operation took [0-9.]+ms/Operation took <time>ms/' "$1" ; }
< 
< ladder_compare () {
<     local B="$1" N="$2" key
<     awk -F'\t' '
<       function rank(p,   r) { r["parse"]=1; r["disambiguate"]=2; r["typecheck"]=3; r["codegen"]=4;
<                               r["link"]=5; r["run"]=6; r["pass"]=7; return r[p] + 0 }
<       FNR == NR { if (FNR > 1) b[$1 "/" $2] = $4 ; next }
<       FNR > 1 {
<           k = $1 "/" $2
<           if (!(k in b))                  { print "NEW\t" k "\t" $4 ; next }
<           if (rank($4) < rank(b[k]))      { print "DOWN\t" k "\t" b[k] " -> " $4 }
<           else if (rank($4) > rank(b[k])) { print "UP\t" k "\t" b[k] " -> " $4 }
<       }' "$B/ladder.tsv" "$N/ladder.tsv"
<     tail -n +2 "$B/pass-list.txt" | cut -f1 | while IFS= read -r key ; do
<         [ -n "$key" ] || continue
<         if [ ! -f "$N/raw/$key.run" ] ; then printf 'MISSING\t%s\n' "$key" ; continue ; fi
<         if ! diff -q <(ladder_filter "$B/raw/$key.run") <(ladder_filter "$N/raw/$key.run") >/dev/null ; then
<             printf 'STDOUT\t%s\n' "$key"
<             diff <(ladder_filter "$B/raw/$key.run") <(ladder_filter "$N/raw/$key.run") | sed 's/^/    /' | head -8
<         fi
<     done
< }
< 
< mg_phases () { awk -F'|' '/^\| *[0-9]+ *\| *`/ { gsub(/[` ]/, "", $3); gsub(/ /, "", $4); print $3 "\t" $4 }' "$1" ; }

#!/bin/bash
# The full gate, once, on the main tree with the walker split (a0205c127) and row 680's line:
# the skill's gate.md steps with the batch workflow's gate role (count and distance stages,
# the distance beside the suites). Scratch: not committed.
cd /home/user/fortress && mkdir -p tmp
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH
export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD FORTRESS_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$PWD/tmp"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh
L=tmp/gate-batch-15b ; O=$L/out
step () { echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" ; }

# From the batch workflow's gate role (explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js, steps 6 and 8).
ATOMIC_OTHER="atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2"
ATOMIC_COMPILER="AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG"
atomic_runs () {
    local O="$1" p d i out rc
    case "$O" in /*) ;; *) O="$PWD/$O" ;; esac
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || return 1
    for p in $ATOMIC_COMPILER $ATOMIC_OTHER ; do
        case " $ATOMIC_COMPILER " in *" $p "*) d=compiler_tests ;; *) d=other_compiler_tests ;; esac
        [ -f "$d/$p.fss" ] || { echo "# atomic $p ABSENT" >> "$O" ; continue ; }
        if ! timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile "$d/$p.fss" >/dev/null 2>&1 ; then
            echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" >> "$O" ; continue
        fi
        for i in 1 2 3 ; do
            out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run "$p" 2>&1) ; rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 124 ] ; then
                out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run "$p" 2>&1) ; rc=$?
                [ "$rc" -eq 124 ] && { echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 TIMEOUT-TWICE" >> "$O" ; continue ; }
            fi
            case "$out" in
              *FAIL*) echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 FAIL" >> "$O" ;;
              *PASS*) echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 PASS" >> "$O" ;;
              *)      echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 NO-PASS rc=$rc" >> "$O" ;;
            esac
        done
    done
    ! grep -q 'FAIL\|TIMEOUT-TWICE\|NO-PASS\|COMPILE-FAILED' "$O"
}
last_landed_checker_count () {
    git -C "$FORTRESS_HOME" log --name-only --pretty=format: -- \
        'explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/checker-count.txt' \
        'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/checker-count.txt' | grep -m1 'checker-count.txt$'
}
checker_compare () {
    local was now wasc nowc bad=0 decl="${3:-none}"
    was=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$1")
    now=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$2")
    wasc=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#crash" { print $2 }' "$1")
    nowc=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#crash" { print $2 }' "$2")
    [ -n "$now" ] || { echo "NO TOTAL   the table has no #total row" ; return 1 ; }
    if [ "$now" -gt "$was" ] ; then echo "COUNT UP   $was -> $now, declared $decl"
    elif [ "$now" -lt "$was" ] ; then echo "COUNT DOWN   $was -> $now, declared $decl"
    else echo "COUNT SAME   $now, declared $decl" ; fi
    if [ "$nowc" != "$wasc" ] ; then
        if [ -n "${4:-}" ] && [ "$nowc" = "$4" ] ; then echo "CRASH DECLARED   $wasc -> $nowc"
        else echo "CRASH CHANGED   $wasc -> $nowc" ; bad=1 ; fi
    fi
    case "$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#shadow" { print $2 }' "$2")" in
      STALE*) echo "SHADOW STALE   the instrumented StaticChecker copy no longer matches the tracked one" ; bad=1 ;;
    esac
    diff "$1" "$2" | sed 's/^/    /'
    [ "$bad" = 0 ]
}

step "0 tree" ; git log --oneline -1 ; git status --short ; uptime ; ps aux | grep -c '[j]ava'
step "1 disk" ; df -h / | tail -1
rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS $L && mkdir -p $L $O

step "2 compileAll"
ant compileAll > $L/compileAll.txt 2>&1 ; echo "compileAll rc=$?"
grep -h '^BUILD\|Caches .*default_repository' $L/compileAll.txt

step "2b distance stage started in the background"
( DS=$(date +%s) ; explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh $O/distance.txt $L/distance ; rc=$? ; echo "distance wall secs=$(( $(date +%s) - DS ))" ; echo EXIT=$rc ) > $L/distance.txt 2>&1 &
DPID=$!

step "3 library order if the caches were emptied, then the ladder's two copies"
if grep -q 'default_repository/caches started again, empty' $L/compileAll.txt ; then
  ( cd ProjectFortress && for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
      echo "== $f" ; ../bin/fortress compile $f ; echo "rc=$?" ; done ; ls ../default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/ ) > $L/library.txt 2>&1
  echo "library order ran" ; grep 'rc=' $L/library.txt
fi
ls default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/
D=$PWD/$L/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

step "4 testFast" ; ant testFast > $L/testFast.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testFast rc=$?"
step "4 testSystem" ; ant testSystem > $L/testSystem.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testSystem rc=$?"
step "4 testSpecData" ; ant testSpecData > $L/testSpecData.txt 2>&1 ; echo "testSpecData rc=$?"

step "5 summary and comparison"
gate_summary $L $O/summary.txt "gate batch 15b"
LS=$(last_landed_summary) ; echo "last landed summary: $LS"
gate_compare "$LS" $O/summary.txt > $L/gate-compare.txt ; echo "gate_compare rc=$?" ; cat $L/gate-compare.txt

step "6 atomic runs"
( atomic_runs $O/summary.txt ) ; echo "atomic rc=$?"
grep -c '^# atomic.*PASS$' $O/summary.txt
grep '^# atomic' $O/summary.txt | grep -v 'PASS$'

step "7 ladder regression"
B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
    -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
    -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
    -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt
{ bash $D/run-subset.sh ; echo "run-subset rc=$?" ; python3 $D/classify.py ; echo "classify rc=$?" ;
  bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh ; echo "microgpt-phase.sh rc=$?" ; python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py ; echo "microgpt-phase.py rc=$?" ; } > $L/ladder.txt 2>&1
grep 'rc=' $L/ladder.txt
ladder_compare $B $D > $L/ladder-comparison.txt 2>&1
diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md) > $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt 2>&1
cat $L/ladder-comparison.txt $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt | sed 's/^/# ladder /' >> $O/summary.txt
mkdir -p $O/ladder
cp $D/ladder.tsv $D/microgpt-phase.md $O/ladder/
cp $L/ladder-comparison.txt $O/ladder/comparison.txt
cp $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt $O/ladder/microgpt-comparison.txt
echo "ladder lines:" ; cat $L/ladder-comparison.txt $L/ladder-mg-comparison.txt

step "8 checker count" ; uptime ; ps aux | grep '[j]ava' | wc -l
CS=$(date +%s)
explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh $O/checker-count.txt $L/checker-count > $L/checker-count.txt 2>&1 ; echo "checker-count rc=$? secs=$(( $(date +%s) - CS ))"
LC=$(last_landed_checker_count) ; echo "last landed count: $LC"
checker_compare "$LC" $O/checker-count.txt "15b: 39" > $L/checker-compare.txt ; echo "checker_compare rc=$?"
sed 's/^/# checker /' $L/checker-compare.txt >> $O/summary.txt
cat $L/checker-compare.txt

step "9 distance stage: wait"
wait $DPID
tail -4 $L/distance.txt
LD=$(git -C "$FORTRESS_HOME" log --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/distance.txt' 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/distance.txt' | grep -m1 'distance.txt$')
echo "last landed distance: $LD"
explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh "$LD" $O/distance.txt > $L/distance-compare.txt 2>&1
sed 's/^/# distance /' $L/distance-compare.txt >> $O/summary.txt
cat $L/distance-compare.txt

step "done"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md against the tree: which standalone
# notes are missing a line, which lines name a file that is gone, which lines
# fall outside the set the index is meant to cover, and which paths named in a
# line's prose no longer resolve. Read-only. Exit 1 if the first two are
# non-empty.
#
# The note set is every *.md under explorations/ except run/experiment trees
# (which document themselves in their own README) and evidence directories.
# Edit the two lists below when the shape of the tree changes.

set -uo pipefail

root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
index="$root/explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md"
[ -f "$index" ] || { echo "no INDEX.md at $index" >&2; exit 2; }

# Run/experiment trees: a directory holding one run's sources and evidence.
run_roots='apl|astra|blinded-fable|compile-ladder|run-b|run-b2|run-c|run-c3|run-c4|fortify|ci|experiment'
# Generic evidence directory names, at any depth.

**Commits** (on `bc65431d5`)
- `a0205c127`: the walker split. `fix.patch` applied cleanly with `git apply`. `ant compileAll` regenerated `FortressAst.scala` byte for byte the same as the patch's file (`cmp` printed nothing). Includes `WalkerJUTest`.
- `c23b49a18`: ledger row 730, the walker that the JVM never compiled, closed by `a0205c127`.
- `e4dabaa0c`: row 680's line at `Decls.scala:414` (`makeTryChecker(this)` becomes `makeTryChecker(newChecker)`).
  - `LocalFunctionSiblingInLoop` and `LocalFunctionSiblingCall` are promoted; each file now equals its text before the hold (`e75bb538b^`).
  - `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn` is re-keyed to 'reference cycle'.
- `7377247d2`: row 680 closed by `e4dabaa0c` with the corrected claim from `climb-batch-15/RECORD.md:155`.
- `3cf18a2b3`: the gate's tables in `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/gate/` (`summary.txt`, `checker-count.txt`, `distance.txt`, `ladder/`).
  - `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv` was overwritten from the gate and is byte-identical to batch 15's, so there was nothing to commit for it.
- `f97c39479`: `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/RECORD.md` and its line in `explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md`. `check-index.sh` exits 0: nothing missing, no file gone.

**Test first**
- **The split:** the failing and passing runs are cited from the probe's section 8 and `SKEPTIC.md` section 3. On the built tree here, `ant testOnly -DtestPattern=WalkerJUTest` gave "Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0".
- **Row 680:** on `a0205c127`'s code, `junit.sh` gave "Tests run: 3, Failures: 3": the two typecheck crashes and "Saw wrong failure" for the recursive case. With the line, "OK (3 tests)", the recursive case now refused with "...because it has reference cycle".

**The gate:** green, one background script, 2026-10-14 23:50:15 to 2026-10-15 00:09:43 UTC, run on `7377247d2`. Each stage against the expectations:

| Stage | Expected | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Suite counts | batch 15's, plus `WalkerJUTest` | compiler 1,212, library 86, othercompiler 263, misc 427 (batch 15's 423 plus `WalkerJUTest`'s 4), `testSystem` 621, `testSpecData` 130; no failure |
| The three tests | promoted or re-keyed | two typecheck "OK", one "Saw expected failure"; one case each, so the count does not change |
| `gate_compare` | no line | no line |
| Atomic runs | 42 PASS | 42 PASS |
| Ladder and microGPT components | unmoved | unmoved |
| Count table | `#total 39`, `#locations 38`, `#crash none`, every api 0 | as expected; "COUNT UP 1 -> 39, declared 15b: 39" |
| Count time | about 352 s | **325 s** |
| Distance | 49, Array3's crash row gone, no site come | 49, crash row gone, `errors.tsv` byte-identical to the landed per-site list |
| Distance time | about 931 s, `FortressLibrary` 462 s | **1,075 s, `FortressLibrary` 628 s** |

The count's table matches the skeptic's idle run with both changes byte for byte, and so does its whole 178-line checker output once the tree path is masked.

The two times are findings, not explained:
- **Count, 325 s**, is below the expected 352 s. The distance stage was still running beside it for its first 243 s, and the run started at load 4.76.
- **Distance, 1,075 s**, is 15 % above the expected 931 s, and `FortressLibrary` 36 % above. It ran beside the suites, from load 0.68 to 6.80, so it is not a pair with the probe's idle run.

**Ledger**
- **Row 730 (new):** section 15, `FIXED`, `implementation gap (checker)`. Its reproducer is `WalkerJUTest.java`; its notes say `fixed a0205c127`.
- **Row 680:** closed with the corrected claim. Its reproducer is `LocalFunctionSiblingInLoop.test`.
- **Row 488's note was refused** by `ledger.py`: "notes-length: 1323 characters; at most 700". The row's notes already use 686 of 700 characters, so no pointer fits. The note's full text is in RECORD.md, "Ledger rows written".
- `ledger.py check --base HEAD`: only the base's ten known failures.

**Decisions** (each is in RECORD.md)
1. **Row 680's line only.** I left out rung C's two-line comment, which reversing `e75bb538b`'s hunk would bring back. The probe and the skeptic measured the line alone.
2. **The recursive test's comment is rewritten.** It named the crash, which the re-keyed test no longer checks. It now says the function gets the reference-cycle refusal, with no citation, as the skeptic left it.
3. **Row 730 went in as one `ledger.py add`, already `FIXED`.** `close` only takes a test under the test folders, and `WalkerJUTest` is under `src/`. This follows row 409's form, so the row has no history entry.
4. **Row 730's class is `checker`.** The template has no generator area, and the time the probe measured is the checker's.
5. **No microGPT walk check.** The skill's `gate.md` adds those lines only when the brief asks for them. 13b ran them; if they are wanted, the summary needs them added.

**For the coordinator and the curator**
- Nothing is pushed: `origin/main..main` lists only my six commits.
- FACTS is not edited, as the brief says. The landed figures for "The true distance to the switch-over" (still 49) and "The checker-count stage's table" (now 39, in `climb-batch-15b/gate/`) are yours to write.
- The probe's FACTS hand-overs are still owed: its section 11, items 1 to 3.
- **Possible gap:** with row 680 closed, the `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn` expected failure has no open ledger row. It now pins the checker's 'reference cycle' refusal, the team's rule for a top-level function in a cycle, as their test `XXX5bn` shows.
- Scratch logs are in `/home/user/fortress/tmp/land15b/` and `/home/user/fortress/tmp/gate-batch-15b/`.
